recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No further FHIR-core source work is needed for FHIR-14328 unless a future terminology-page review chooses to make broader, unrelated wording changes.
issue_request: FHIR-14328 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 correction for the FHIR-core terminologies page. It reported that the sentence "When codes are carried in resources, one of 4 different data types is used:" was followed by a list whose count could be read as either three or six datatypes, so the misleading numeric count needed to be fixed.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git commit 713d861e1c5be7055da8987b47109f211cb12996, matching the Jira comment that cites svn revision 13377. That commit changed source/terminologies.html from "one of 4 different data types" to "one of several different data types".
additional_context: The current build-source page source/terminologies.html now says "one of several different datatypes". Later commit 8592e1207273b786db340efb927bb6d1dc9756c9 only normalized spelling from "data types" to "datatypes" while preserving the corrected count wording. Jira search found only the seed issue, Zulip search found bot notifications for issue creation and the implementation commit, and Confluence searches found no conflicting record.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The current checkout no longer contains the stale "one of 4" wording and already uses the corrected non-numeric phrasing requested by FHIR-14328.
